title: Kiro Pricing (2026): Every Plan and Credit Cost
summary: Kiro pricing includes Free, Pro, Pro+, and Pro Max plans with different credit allowances. Compare plans to choose the one matching your monthly usage.
body_markdown:
## What Kiro costs at realistic team usage


If four developers use Kiro, the bill is the per-seat price times four, plus overage on every credit they burn past what the plans include. The overage line is the one your weekly measurement controls.


Credits are the metered unit, so each plan gets judged on the same five criteria:


- Monthly price per seat
- Included credits
- Overage rate per credit
- Number of seats
- What happens when credits run out


Of those five, the first and fourth set the floor of the bill. The second, third and fifth decide how far above that floor you land.


### Kiro monthly cost for a four-developer team


Take one team building one product for a month, with each developer using Kiro on most working days.


Multiply the weekly credit count you measured by the weeks in a month, then compare that total with the included credits across all four seats, revealing whether you're within your allocation. Whatever is left over is billed at the overage rate.


Check whether included credits are pooled or stay with each seat, because one heavy user can overrun an individual allowance while the team as a whole stays under.


### Light, daily and heavy users compared


At the light end, a user may never touch the overage rate, and a daily user sits near the allowance. A heavy user crosses it early and pays the per-credit rate for the rest of the month.


Price each person's burn rather than averaging the team, because four people rarely behave alike. An average hides the one seat that generates most of the overage.


### Where the cheapest plan becomes the expensive one


Once your burn passes the point where the two lines cross, a cheap plan with a small credit allowance and a steep overage rate costs more than a pricier plan.


Pick a more demanding model instead of Auto and the credits each task consumes multiply, so the same week of work lands on a different plan. Model choice moves that point.


Find your crossover from measured credits and the overage rate. Then check what the plan does when credits run out, because a hard stop and automatic overage billing lead to different kinds of surprise.
